curiosities: It launched in 1977 alongside the Apple II and Commodore PET, a trio of early home computers.
Tandy sold it through its RadioShack stores.
Its processor is a Z80 at 1.77 MHz.
The first model came with 4 KB, a monitor and a cassette recorder for $599.
Scott Adams's Adventureland, one of the first commercial adventure games, began on it.
